title: Column visibility lens and adaptive density presets for large virtual tables
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Our virtual table is difficult to inspect and personalize at high column density. Users ask for a fast, non-destructive way to locate, preview, and toggle columns without breaking virtualization or losing layout. They also want to save density/compactness preferences per workspace. Goal: Introduce a transient 'column visibility lens' (keyboard+mouse+touch) that highlights and previews columns, and add adaptive density presets (snapshots of spacing, font-size tokens, and column compression rules) that users can apply and persist per view. This should work with existing column resizing, pinned columns, virtualization, and sorting/filtering affordances.
proposal: 1) Column visibility lens: an overlay activated via hotkey ("V") or toolbar button that dims non-target columns, shows a compact header-only preview for each column, and exposes quick toggles to hide/show columns. The lens supports fuzzy search of column names, keyboard navigation (arrow keys to move lens focus), and SR announcements when a column is toggled. 2) Adaptive density presets: allow 3 default presets (Comfortable, Compact, Dense) plus user-defined snapshots. Each preset bundles token overrides for row height, spacing, type scale, and a column compression profile (min-width thresholds, prioritize collapse order). Presets can be saved per table and placed into the view drop-down. 3) Integration: Ensure lens actions are virtualized-safe (no full-row render), resizing from the lens updates persisted column widths, and presets trigger an animated reflow that respects virtualization chunking.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: We will use the existing token system for density overrides to keep theme parity but need a small set of transient tokens for animated reflow.
Lens rendering: implement header-focused virtual rendering to avoid expensive body reflow; trade visual fidelity for performance when >200 columns.
Accessibility: SR announcements and keyboard-only flows increase complexity but are required for compliance; testing will need screen reader verification.
Persistence scope: per-user vs per-workspace decisions are product-level and will be gated behind settings; MVP uses per-view per-user persistence.
Edge cases: pinned columns and frozen groups must remain visible; hiding a pinned column should require confirmation or auto-unpin policy.
acceptance_criteria: Activating the lens (hotkey or toolbar) overlays the table and allows fuzzy search/filtering of column names without rerendering all rows.
Toggling column visibility via the lens updates the table immediately and persists the choice for the view session.
Three built-in density presets apply token overrides and compression rules with <200ms perceived reflow on standard test dataset (50k rows, 80 columns) on supported browsers.
Keyboard-only flow: navigate lens with arrows, toggle with Space/Enter, and exit with Esc; screen readers announce column name and visibility state changes.
Resizing a column through the lens/resizer updates persisted width and plays a performant animation that does not block scrolling or request handling.
Unit and E2E tests cover virtualization safety: lens operations do not break continuous scroll or produce visual artifacts when chunks are loading.
implementation_notes: Engineering should implement a header-only virtual renderer for the lens overlay and expose a compact API for token overrides. Use existing column-metadata model to store visibility and compression priority. Runtime should guard animations when chunk-loading is active. Work with infra to add a telemetry event for preset-apply and lens-usage to measure adoption.
comments: 2025-02-18 Sofia Patel: Kickoff - collected feedback from support & a quick survey of power users. High-level prototype attached. Prioritize accessibility and non-destructive toggles.
2025-02-20 Liam Chen: Reviewed feasibility with frontend; header-only virtualization approach looks viable. Need engineering spike to measure render cost for 200+ columns.
2025-02-22 Design crit: reduce microcopy on lens toggles and add confirmation for hiding pinned columns. Also recommend default 'Compact' preset to avoid layout breakage for narrow viewports.
2025-02-24 PM feedback (Nora Ramirez): Requesting per-workspace persistence as stretch; ok to ship MVP per-user. Add telemetry for preset changes and lens activations.
2025-02-27 Liam Chen: Spike results: header-only overlay renders <16ms for 200 columns on MacBook Pro; body virtualization unaffected. Moving to planned.
2025-02-27 Sofia Patel: Updated acceptance criteria with performance numbers and accessibility checks.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): implement lens and three presets, per-user persistence, keyboard + SR support, telemetry. Release behind feature flag. Phase 2: workspace persistence, preset sharing, AI-suggested compressed profiles, and analytics dashboard to show adoption. Roll out to 10% canary for 2 weeks, monitor errors, latency, and preset application events before broader rollout.
